messages:
Anika: Quick thread — proposal to simplify the implicit fallback + affinity smoothing logic in the policy engine. TL;DR: remove automatic weight drift and replace with an explicit `fallback_quota` DSL field + a compatible runtime shim. Want to align on risk/migration plan.

Ethan: +1 for making the behavior explicit. The current smoothing surprises tenants during bursts. Can you sketch backwards compatibility?

Anika: Sketch: policies that don't specify `fallback_quota` get a shim mapping current implicit behavior -> `fallback_quota: calculated:legacy` so runtimes keep old behavior for now. New opt-in semantics will use `fallback_quota: explicit` if set.

Priya: Important: telemetry will need new counters. Right now we only emit "fallback_invoked" and aggregate weight deltas. We should add: `fallback_quota_assigned`, `fallback_used`, `fallback_evicted_reason`.

Marco: We should also capture the probe latency window and capacity signal when fallback fires. Otherwise teams will see quota churn with no signal context.

Devon: Operational point: any change that can increase hedging/fallbacks will spike GPU usage. We need a canary plan with a budget cap. Maybe rate-limit fallback throughput per-tenant during canary.

Anika: Agreed. Proposed rollout phases: 1) policy compiler emits shim for legacy policies, 2) runtime adds new metric emissions + sampling hooks, 3) canary switch (policy flag) for 5% of traffic with hard fallback throughput cap, 4) enable for groups after evaluation.

Ethan: For the runtime shim, do we prefer sidecar translation (compiler->sidecar) or compile-time expansion into policy json? Sidecar easier for fast rollback.

Priya: Sidecar also centralizes metric tagging, but adds another hot path. If sidecar is on the critical path we must benchmark.

Marco: Another option: compile-time expansion + feature flag that toggles whether runtime reads `fallback_quota`. That yields lowest latency hit but requires a safe migration step.

Anika: Good tradeoff list. My preference is sidecar translation for the canary window (fast toggle), then once stable, bake expansion into compiled policies. Keeps rollback simple.

Devon: Ops request: add an emergency kill switch at the router level to set `fallback_quota=0` for a tenant. We had a past incident where noisy tenant used fallback aggressively and ate burst capacity.

Ethan: Implementation sketch (policy DSL example):
```
# before
policies:
  - id: my-route
    soft_preferences:
      - prefer: low_latency
    fallback: implicit

# after (explicit)
policies:
  - id: my-route
    soft_preferences:
      - prefer: low_latency
    fallback_quota:
      mode: explicit
      budget_per_min: 10
      burst: 2
```

Priya: Nice. For `calculated:legacy` shim we need a deterministic mapping function (input: historical fallback rate, tenant tier, region). We should include that mapping in compiler tests.

Marco: Also add a simulation harness step: run the new policy semantics through the routing simulator with historical traces (last 30 days). Compare cost/latency deltas and produce an alert if cost delta > 15% or p99 latency > baseline + 50ms.

Anika: Agreed. We'll add a dry-run telemetry reporter that writes simulation vs production diffs to a retention stream.

Devon: Canary controls: ops needs token-bucket limits on fallback tokens consumed per-minute and an account-level kill switch. We can encode that as runtime config separate from compiled policy so ops can adjust mid-canary.

Ethan: Policy engine interface change note: expose new hook `on_fallback_eval(context) -> token_grant` so external admission controllers (e.g., quota service) can veto or throttle fallback decisions. Keep default no-op to preserve behavior.

Priya: Security/compliance: ensure the new telemetry doesn't accidentally include tenant prompt content. Metrics must be aggregate only and hashed ids.

Anika: Yep — metrics will be counts and latency distributions only, tenant_id will be hashed and salted per-region. No prompt text.

Marco: Timeline proposal:
- Week 1: design doc + mapping function and test plans
- Week 2-3: implement sidecar shim + telemetry emissions + unit tests
- Week 4: simulation harness + run against replay traces
- Week 5: small canary (1-5% traffic) with ops caps
- Week 6-8: progressive rollout by tenant cohort

Devon: Ops checklist: alert thresholds, cost budget enforcements wired to billing pipeline, emergency toggle endpoint, runbook updated. Also coordinate with sales for enterprise tenants if quota changes might impact SLAs.

Ethan: One more risk: some older runtime shards assume monotonic weight decay. If we remove smoothing behavior too early it could destabilize affinity heuristics. Need unit & integration tests specifically for shard-level admission behavior.

Anika: Good catch. We'll add a fuzz test that varies weight deltas and ensures admission decisions don't oscillate wildly.

Priya: I'll own telemetry schema + compiler tests. Ethan/Marco you own sidecar + simulator. Devon will own ops canary controls. Anika will shepherd the RFC and rollout.

ops-bot: Deploy report stub created: runbook: https://internal/runbooks/fallback-quota-rollout | canary-channel: eng-runtime | budget: ops-budget-2028

Anika: Thanks — will draft the RFC with the above plan and ping for review. If nobody objects I'll post the formal doc by EOD. :thumbsup:
